title: Accurate Probabilities for Higher-Order Differentials
summary: The known probability-1 case for higher-order differentials follows from a degree limit; determining accurate probabilities beyond it without prohibitively large Boolean-function evaluations remains open.

formal_statement.body: In differential cryptanalysis, determine accurate probabilities for higher-order differentials when evaluating the associated Boolean functions would require prohibitively many terms. The unresolved task is to obtain these probabilities without that prohibitively expensive evaluation, enabling higher-order differentials to be used beyond cases with probability 1, where a derivative of a certain order must evaluate to zero because of a limit on the function's degree.

scope.domain: The domain is differential cryptanalysis, specifically the probability analysis of higher-order differentials.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine accurate probabilities for higher-order differentials without evaluating associated Boolean functions with prohibitively many terms, extending their use beyond probability-1 cases.

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents the issue as an open problem in differential cryptanalysis and attributes the difficulty of determining accurate higher-order differential probabilities to prohibitively large Boolean-function evaluations. It notes that the common use case is the probability-1 setting arising from a degree limit.
citation_labels: Tyge Tiessen et al., Polytopic Cryptanalysis
